1 📥 Loading libraries.

Loading Necessary libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(dplyr)
library(grid)
library(scales)
library(ggtext)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggthemes)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)

2 📥 Loading and Preparing the Data.

2.1 Load the Data set.

Read The Data set

data<- read.csv("C:/Users/Earnest/Desktop/School of Statistician/week16_time_series_dashboard_data.csv")

2.2 Convert date to proper format and extract day of the week.

data$date <- as.Date(data$date)
data$day_of_week <- weekdays(data$date)

3 Sales & Demand Analysis.

3.1 Which regions recorded the highest number of orders in week 16?.

Total Orders by Region

orders_by_region <- data %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(total_orders = sum(orders)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_orders))

print(orders_by_region)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   region      total_orders
##   <chr>              <int>
## 1 Central           120378
## 2 Nairobi           119865
## 3 Rift Valley       119505
## 4 Coast             119330
## 5 Western           118838

Visualization

ggplot(orders_by_region, aes(x = reorder(region, -total_orders), y = total_orders, fill = region)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  labs(title = "Total Orders by Region - Week 16",
       x = "Region", y = "Total Orders") +
  theme_minimal()

3.2 How do orders differ between Online and Store chanenels for each product Category?

orders_by_category_channel <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category, channel) %>%
  summarise(total_orders = sum(orders)) %>%
  spread(channel, total_orders) %>%
  mutate(difference = Online - Store)


print(orders_by_category_channel)
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
## # Groups:   product_category [5]
##   product_category Online Store difference
##   <chr>             <int> <int>      <int>
## 1 Apparel           65791 60242       5549
## 2 Beauty            60499 54764       5735
## 3 Electronics       43847 39904       3943
## 4 Groceries         87893 79613       8280
## 5 Home              55230 50133       5097

Visualization

ggplot(data, aes(x = product_category, y = orders, fill = channel)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Orders by Product Category and Channel", 
       x = "Product Category", y = "Total Orders") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

3.3 Which product category had the most units sold, and in which region?

units_by_category_region <- data %>%

  group_by(product_category, region) %>%
  summarise(total_units = sum(units)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_units))

print(head(units_by_category_region, 10))
## # A tibble: 10 × 3
## # Groups:   product_category [2]
##    product_category region      total_units
##    <chr>            <chr>             <int>
##  1 Groceries        Nairobi           52861
##  2 Groceries        Central           52671
##  3 Groceries        Coast             52598
##  4 Groceries        Rift Valley       52453
##  5 Groceries        Western           52016
##  6 Apparel          Rift Valley       41773
##  7 Apparel          Coast             41651
##  8 Apparel          Nairobi           41627

Find the maximum

max_units <- units_by_category_region[1, ]
cat("Category with most units:", max_units$product_category, 
    "in region:", max_units$region, 
    "with", max_units$total_units, "units\n")
## Category with most units: Groceries in region: Nairobi with 52861 units

3.4 Are there noticeable daily sales trends?

daily_trends <- data %>%
  group_by(date, day_of_week) %>%
  summarise(daily_orders = sum(orders),

Visualization

ggplot(daily_trends, aes(x = date, y = daily_orders)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +

       x = "Date", y = "Total Orders") +
  theme_minimal()

Explanation

“What’s selling, where, and when?” Measures basic business activity - orders, units sold, and daily patterns across regions and channels.

4 Revenue & Profitability

4.1 Which region generated the highest total revenue?

revenue_by_region <- data %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue)) %>%

  arrange(desc(total_revenue))

print(revenue_by_region)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   region      total_revenue
##   <chr>               <dbl>
## 1 Nairobi         12274034.
## 2 Coast           12191615.
## 3 Central         12005573.
## 4 Rift Valley     11993027.
## 5 Western         11966350.

Visualization

ggplot(revenue_by_region, aes(x = reorder(region, -total_revenue), y = total_revenue, fill = region)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Total Revenue by Region - Week 16", 
       x = "Region", y = "Total Revenue") +
  theme_minimal()

4.2 Most profitable product category

profit_by_category <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category) %>%
  summarise(total_profit = sum(profit),
            profit_margin = sum(profit) / 

sum(revenue) * 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_profit))

print(profit_by_category)
## # A tibble: 5 × 3
##   product_category total_profit profit_margin
##   <chr>                   <dbl>         <dbl>
## 1 Electronics          7424296.          22.0
## 2 Home                 3983610.          40.0
## 3 Apparel              3667551.          45.0
## 4 Beauty               2304960.          50.0
## 5 Groceries            1498434.          38.0

4.3 Profit margin across categories and channels

margin_by_category_channel <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category, channel) %>%
  summarise(profit_margin = sum(profit) / sum(revenue) * 100) %>%
  spread(channel, profit_margin)

print(margin_by_category_channel)
## # A tibble: 5 × 3
## # Groups:   product_category [5]
##   product_category Online Store
##   <chr>             <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 Apparel            45.0  45.0
## 2 Beauty             50.0  50.0
## 3 Electronics        21.9  22.0
## 4 Groceries          38.0  38.0
## 5 Home               40.0  40.0

Visualization

ggplot(data, aes(x = product_category, y = profit/revenue*100, fill = channel)) +
  geom_boxplot() +

  labs(title = "Profit Margin by Product Category and Channel", 
       x = "Product Category", y = "Profit Margin (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

4.4 Online vs Store Average Order Value (AOV)

aov_comparison <- data %>%
  group_by(channel) %>%
  summarise(avg_order_value = mean(avg_order_value),
            total_orders = sum(orders))

print(aov_comparison)
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   channel avg_order_value total_orders
##   <chr>             <dbl>        <int>
## 1 Online             126.       313260
## 2 Store              125.       284656

Statistical test

t_test_result <- t.test(avg_order_value ~ channel, data = data)
print(t_test_result)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  avg_order_value by channel
## t = 0.20195, df = 4997.5, p-value = 0.84
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Online and group Store is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -7.388463  9.085471
## sample estimates:
## mean in group Online  mean in group Store 
##             125.6027             124.7542

Explanation

“Where is the money coming from and how profitable is it?” Tracks actual money earned and profit margins, showing which areas truly drive your bottom line.

segment_analysis <- data %>%
  group_by(region, product_category) %>%

5.2 Regional category preferences

regional_preferences <- data %>%
  group_by(region, product_category) %>%
  summarise(revenue_share = sum(revenue)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  mutate(total_region_revenue = sum(revenue_share),
         percentage = revenue_share / total_region_revenue * 100) %>%
  arrange(region, desc(percentage))

print(regional_preferences)

Heatmap visualization

ggplot(regional_preferences, aes(x = region, y = product_category, fill = percentage)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue") +

  labs(title = "Revenue Share by Region and Category", 
       x = "Region", y = "Product Category") +
  theme_minimal()

6 Operational Efficiency & Costs

6.1 Highest cost-to-revenue ratio

cost_efficiency <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category) %>%
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue),
            total_cost = sum(cost),
            cost_ratio = sum(cost) / sum(revenue) * 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(cost_ratio))

print(cost_efficiency)

6.3 Low profit despite high revenue

profitability_analysis <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category) %>%
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue),

            profit_per_order = sum(profit) / sum(orders)) %>%
  arrange(profit_margin)

print(profitability_analysis)

7 Returns & Risk Analysis

7.1 Highest returns rate by category

returns_analysis <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category) %>%
  summarise(avg_returns_rate = mean(returns_rate) * 100,
            total_units = sum(units)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_returns_rate))

print(returns_analysis)
## # A tibble: 5 × 3
##   product_category avg_returns_rate total_units
##   <chr>                       <dbl>       <int>
## 1 Home                         3.05      166108
## 2 Apparel                      3.00      203816
## 3 Groceries                    2.99      262599
## 4 Beauty                       2.98      184197
## 5 Electronics                  2.95      134771

7.2 Correlation between returns rate and AOV

correlation_test <- cor.test(data$returns_rate, data$avg_order_value)

print(correlation_test)
## 
##  Pearson's product-moment correlation
## 
## data:  data$returns_rate and data$avg_order_value
## t = -0.79232, df = 4998, p-value = 0.4282
## alternative hypothesis: true correlation is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.03891379  0.01651784
## sample estimates:
##         cor 
## -0.01120659

Scatter plot

ggplot(data, aes(x = avg_order_value, y = returns_rate * 100)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Returns Rate vs Average Order Value", 
       x = "Average Order Value", y = "Returns Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

7.3 Online vs Store returns comparison

returns_by_channel <- data %>%
  group_by(channel) %>%
  summarise(avg_returns_rate = mean(returns_rate) * 100,

            total_orders = sum(orders))

print(returns_by_channel)
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   channel avg_returns_rate total_orders
##   <chr>              <dbl>        <int>
## 1 Online              3.00       313260
## 2 Store               2.98       284656

Statistical test

t_test_returns <- t.test(returns_rate ~ channel, data = data)
print(t_test_returns)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  returns_rate by channel
## t = 0.61284, df = 4996.5, p-value = 0.54
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Online and group Store is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.0003820916  0.0007296116
## sample estimates:
## mean in group Online  mean in group Store 
##           0.03001216           0.02983840

Explanation

“Where are we losing money and why?” Focuses on product returns and risks that eat into profits, highlighting quality or customer satisfaction issues.

8.3 Cost reduction and profitability recommendations

Identify improvement opportunities

improvement_opportunities <- data %>%
  group_by(product_category, region) %>%
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue),
            total_profit = sum(profit),
            profit_margin = sum(profit) / sum(revenue) * 100,
            avg_returns = mean(returns_rate) * 100,

            cost_ratio = sum(cost) / sum(revenue) * 100) %>%
  arrange(profit_margin)

print(improvement_opportunities)
## # A tibble: 25 × 7
## # Groups:   product_category [5]
##    product_category region  total_revenue total_profit profit_margin avg_returns
